message.content: The sea’s “color” isn’t fixed—it shifts across a spectrum from deep indigo‑blue near the horizon to turquoise or even greenish hues closer to shore, especially where algae or phytoplankton thrive. In clear open water it often looks sky‑blued because sunlight scatters off the surface and deeper layers absorb longer wavelengths (red/orange). Near coastlines, suspended particles, sediment, and marine life tint the water toward greens or browns. So while we usually think of the ocean as blue, its true palette depends on depth, clarity, light angle, and biological activity.
